industry.why: Double Underweight, carried unchanged. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the United States consumer surveys fell again (University of Michigan 46.3 preliminary October, down 1.8; Conference Board 81.9 in September, down 6.7; Goldman Sachs 19 Oct), consumer discretionary lagged with technology and communication services in the week's rotation (Jefferies, 17 Oct), and the European consumer was again not read, so the row rests on the US reading and on the regime. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: D now, D prior, the largest industry in the universe at 138 stocks. Counter-case: Retail physical reads B and Online retail A on relative strength, Hotels C, which is where cheap good businesses accumulate, and a double notch on 138 stocks shuts bottom-up work out of the Lists; the exceptions are carried at sector level (H.3 Neutral).

sector.why: Underweight, carried unchanged. Component 1 regime, 9-Oct-26 (late-cycle rates squeeze turning into a European credit-and-sovereign stress episode: hiking path re-marked up, credit joined rates, French spread 152 basis points, European breadth at three-year lows on all four averages, index 5.3% off its high, defensives turning over one and four weeks but unconfirmed, growth firm at the level; sources present 2026-W41): big-ticket consumer purchases financed at higher rates under a low United States consumer reading; the turning note's falling side has the premium carmakers and suppliers as its widest group (seven of 25 failing the negative test, BMW and Mercedes-Benz each minus 15 points relative over 20 days), with autos not spoken to by any source. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-09 against 2026-08-07, not week on week: F now, F prior. Held at D, not F, because the evidence for a second notch is a brainstorm and because the MI Pool holds no name in this row. Counter-case: the strongest balance sheets are first to be right-sized and first to recover.

geography.why: Underweight, carried unchanged with the reason strengthened. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the spillover from France to Italy is the new fact this week (Goldman, 16 Oct, 'tentative spillover to Italy'), and the Italian listings in the Pool are bank-heavy (Monte dei Paschi, Credito Emiliano, Mediobanca) beside global businesses (Eni, Saipem, Tenaris, STMicroelectronics, Technoprobe, Reply). Not Double Underweight because Goldman also says contagion risk is lower than in 2011-15, its fragmentation index shows risk 'remains limited', and Southern European banks are healthier; relative strength is not graded by country. Moves to F if the fragmentation index rises or the Italian premium is read above 150 basis points; back to C under 100.
